display.text:
# Context Pack: `run-journal-fencing` — Run-control SQLite journal and fencing

Target: ultraplan-go @ 8eef70f4903b25580719960009a170945bdad9ad (frozen; working tree differs only in internal/sprint smoke files, runcontrol+app identical).
Planning context: ultraplan-workspace @ ab12dc38059c9bf485f9aced9075bcd7d924cac5.
Domain: durability-core. Risk: critical. Descriptive only — no defect judgments.

## 1. Purpose

`internal/runcontrol` is the durable identity and arbitration layer for every executing UltraPlan operation (doc.go:1-6). It records: the accepted execution (`runs`), at most one fenced owner attempt per run (`attempts`), a strictly ordered append-only sanitized event journal (`events`), optional operation alias identities for dedup (`operation_aliases`), and reconciliation decision evidence (`reconciliation_log`) — all in one private SQLite database at `.ultraplan/run-control.db`. It deliberately does NOT own product workflow state, artifacts, or runtime supervision (doc.go, interfaces.go:47-48). Core mechanisms: accept-before-execute; fenced claim with lease + heartbeat; cancellation request/acknowledge split across processes; single-winner terminal compare-and-set over seven outcomes including explicit uncertainty (`cleanup_uncertain`, `persistence_degraded`); conservative birth-identity reconciliation that never infers success.

## 2. Entrypoints and control flow

### 2.1 Open path (`sqlite.go:60-134`)
`OpenSQLite(ctx, workspaceRoot, SQLiteOptions)`: validate workspace root (abs, dir, sqlite.go:136-152) → prepare private storage (`preparePrivateDatabase`, :154-191): `.ultraplan/` created 0700, symlink/non-dir rejected via Lstat (:159-165); `run-control.db` created `O_CREATE|O_EXCL|O_RDWR` 0600, symlink/non-regular rejected (:172-186); `enforcePrivateMode` chmods then re-stats to verify exact mode (:193-205) → open DSN with fixed pragmas `_busy_timeout=5000 _foreign_keys=on _journal_mode=WAL _synchronous=FULL _txlock=immediate _defensive=1` (:73-80) → ping, then `verifyPragmas` reads back journal_mode/synchronous/foreign_keys/busy_timeout only (:207-227) → `migrateSchema` (migration.go:25-82; current-version DBs take the lock-free verify path — schema record equality + integrity check; migration itself belongs to surface `run-recovery-retention`) → connection pool default 4, operator-cappable 1..16 (:92-100) → repository assembled with injected-or-wall Clock, RandomIDSource, normalized retention policy (:107-131).

### 2.2 Accept (`sqlite.go:378-470`)
Quota gates first: `storageBytes()` sums sizes of all regular files whose names start with `run-control.db` in `.ultraplan/` (retention.go:35-56 — includes `-wal`/`-shm`/`.migrate.lock`/backups); usage ≥ 80% of hard quota triggers inline `Compact(ctx,64)` (:384-390); usage ≥ soft quota (hard − 16 MiB headroom) refuses acceptance with retryable `CodeQuota` (:391-395). Then Target/Correlation validation, ProductStatus/ConfirmationDigest ≤ MaxSafeValueBytes (:396-404), RunID minted when absent and validated (:405-415), correlation marshaled bounded to 256 KiB (:416). One immediate transaction inserts the `runs` row (lifecycle `accepted`, liveness `unknown`, record_state `full`, cancellation_state `none`, last_sequence 0) (:429-444); duplicate RunID → typed Conflict (:440-442). Optional OperationAlias inserts an `operation_aliases` row in the same tx; alias conflict → Conflict (:445-455). Snapshot loaded + validated inside the tx before commit (:456-462). NOTE: Accept writes NO event row; the journal stays empty until the first cancellation/append/terminal/reconcile write.

### 2.3 Claim (`sqlite.go:486-592`)
Validates RunID/Owner/Correlation/Lease>0 and AttemptID (minted when absent) (:490-512). In one immediate transaction: read lifecycle+current_attempt (:529); terminal run → `CodeTerminal`; existing current attempt → `CodeConflict` "run already has a current owner attempt" (:533-538). Next lifecycle = running, preserved as cancelling if already cancelling (:539-542). Ordinal = MAX(ordinal)+1 and fencing_generation = MAX(fencing_generation)+1 over the run's attempts (:543-546); attempts table enforces `UNIQUE(run_id,ordinal)` and `UNIQUE(run_id,fencing_generation)` (:288-289) plus `fencing_generation > 0` (:278). INSERT attempt (owner_id, host_digest, boot_id, pid, process_birth_token, claimed_at=heartbeat_at=now, lease_expires_at=now+lease) (:547-560), then CAS-style UPDATE of runs: `SET current_attempt_id=?, lifecycle=?, liveness='live', started_at=COALESCE(started_at,?), updated_at=? WHERE run_id=? AND current_attempt_id IS NULL AND terminal_outcome IS NULL`; RowsAffected ≠ 1 → Conflict (:561-571). Snapshot validated pre-commit. Because no code path ever nulls `current_attempt_id`, each run is claimed AT MOST once in its lifetime (grep over package: only setter is sqlite.go:563; reconcile paths require it NULL/non-terminal).

### 2.4 Append (`sqlite.go:608-711`)
Fence validated (RunID+AttemptID grammar, OwnerID non-empty, generation > 0; model.go:287-298) → draft normalized (typed fields copied into payload, model.go:490-505) and sanitized (§6) → hard-quota gate: usage ≥ hard quota rejects all event types except reserved ones (lifecycle/warning/cancellation/recovery/terminal/omission, :618-622, :713-720) → draft validation (:1005-1029: known type/scope, active-only lifecycle hint, stage/task ≤512 bytes without NUL/CR/LF, payload keys ≤128 bytes/values ≤32 KiB without NUL, omission needs positive count). Immediate transaction: `verifyFence` (:985-1003 — attempt row must exist for (run_id, attempt_id), owner_id and fencing_generation must match, and runs.current_attempt_id must equal the fence's attempt) → read last_sequence+lifecycle; terminal run → `CodeTerminal` immutable (:652-658); lifecycle hint must satisfy `validActiveTransition` (:1031-1047: accepted→{queued,running,cancelling}, queued→{running,cancelling}, running→cancelling, cancelling→nothing, self-transitions allowed) → sequence = last_sequence+1 inserted into events (:666-672) → CAS UPDATE runs: `SET last_sequence=?, lifecycle=?, omission_total += ?, updated_at=? WHERE run_id=? AND last_sequence=? AND current_attempt_id=? AND terminal_outcome IS NULL`; RowsAffected ≠ 1 → `CodeStaleFence` "event writer lost its authoritative fence" (:677-686) → inline `compactRunJournal` when the run exceeds 4096 events or 16 MiB retained payload bytes: deletes oldest progress/message/omission events (never the just-written sequence), sets record_state=compacted, history_complete=0, oldest_retained_sequence=MIN(sequence) or last+1; nothing removable → typed `CodeQuota` failure (retention.go:58-95) → snapshot validated, commit, notify (no-op unless Notifier wired; production wires none), debug log.

### 2.5 Heartbeat (`lifecycle.go:14-68`)
Lease > 0 required; hard-quota gate REFUSES heartbeats at ≥ hard quota ("hard quota requires the owner to stop active work", :24-28). Immediate transaction: verifyFence → CAS UPDATE attempts `SET heartbeat_at=?, lease_expires_at=now+lease WHERE ... AND outcome IS NULL` (RowsAffected≠1 → StaleFence) → CAS UPDATE runs liveness='live' where current attempt matches and not terminal (RowsAffected≠1 → StaleFence) → snapshot, commit, metric. Heartbeat both extends the lease and clears a prior `stalled` marking.

### 2.6 Cancellation request / acknowledge split
- RequestCancellation (`lifecycle.go:70-134`): reason trimmed, must be non-empty, ≤32 KiB, no NUL/CR/LF (:77-80); CLI additionally whitelists {user_requested, operator_requested, shutdown_requested, quota_exceeded} (run_commands.go:394-401). No fence required — works ownerless. Idempotent short-circuit: already terminal OR any non-none cancellation state returns (current snapshot, changed=false) after committing the read tx (:91-96). Otherwise inserts a `cancellation` event (attempt_id nullable — set only when a current attempt exists, :102-109) and CAS UPDATEs runs: `SET lifecycle='cancelling', cancellation_state='requested', reason, requested_at, updated_at, last_sequence=? WHERE run_id=? AND terminal_outcome IS NULL AND cancellation_state='none' AND last_sequence=?` (:110-120); lost race → retryable Conflict.
- AcknowledgeCancellation (`lifecycle.go:136-194`): fence-gated. Short-circuits (changed=false) when terminal or already acknowledged; state ≠ requested → Conflict; else inserts an ack `cancellation` event and CAS UPDATEs `cancellation_state='acknowledged', acknowledged_at` guarded by current_attempt match + state=requested + unchanged last_sequence (:156-181).
- `cancellation_state='uncertain'` exists in the schema enum and Health projection but no code path writes it (grep: only model.go definition + Health count sqlite.go:877).

### 2.7 ProposeTerminal (`sqlite.go:722-807`)
The ONLY writer of terminal state (plus reconcileUnclaimed below). Validated proposal (outcome ∈ closed 7-value enum, reason/proposer bounded, :731-736). Immediate transaction: verifyFence → loadSnapshot; if Terminal already present, COMMIT the read tx and return (winner, won=false, nil) — losers observe the incumbent outcome instead of erroring (:753-758). Winner path: insert one `terminal` event at last_sequence+1 (payload {outcome,reason}) (:759-768), then CAS UPDATE runs setting lifecycle=outcome.Lifecycle(), liveness='terminal', finished_at, last_sequence, terminal_* columns `WHERE run_id=? AND current_attempt_id=? AND terminal_outcome IS NULL`; RowsAffected ≠ 1 → StaleFence loser (:769-786); attempts.outcome stamped on the winner's own attempt (:787-790); snapshot validated against the full terminal-consistency rules (model.go:355-364) before commit. Schema CHECK ties terminal_outcome ↔ finished_at ↔ terminal lifecycle (:268-269).

### 2.8 Reconcile (`lifecycle.go:301-416`)
Runs on every repository open (app/run_control.go:66) and every 10 s inside active-operation control loops. Grace defaults to ReconciliationGrace=45 s; batch default 64/max 256. Pass 1 — unclaimed runs (`current_attempt_id IS NULL AND accepted_at older than grace`, :320-339): `reconcileUnclaimed` (:427-479) re-checks state in-tx, inserts one `terminal` event (attempt_id NULL) and CAS-terminalizes to interrupted/"owner_never_claimed_after_grace" guarded by `current_attempt_id IS NULL AND terminal_outcome IS NULL`; concurrent claim/win → silent no-op. Pass 2 — expired owners (runs joined to their current attempt where lease_expires_at older than grace, :360-383): probe recorded PID via ProcessProbe; `reconcileProcessDecision` matrix (:481-495):
- ErrProcessNotFound → interrupted, "owner_process_missing_after_grace";
- other probe error → cleanup_uncertain, "owner_process_identity_uncertain_after_grace";
- incomplete stored OR observed identity fields → cleanup_uncertain;
- exact field mismatch (host/boot/pid/birth) → interrupted, "owner_process_birth_mismatch_after_grace";
- exact live match → NO terminal: markStalled only (:497-509, liveness='stalled' CAS on still-current attempt; StaleFence tolerated).
Terminal proposals ride the DEAD attempt's own recorded fence (ProposedBy="reconciler"); ErrTerminal/ErrStaleFence from racing writers are tolerated (:392, :401). Every decision appended to reconciliation_log via recordReconciliation (:511-527; evidence reduced to class strings safe_identity_only / acceptance_timestamp_only; errors deliberately ignored by callers `_ = r.recordReconciliation(...)` :352, :411). Report counters Scanned/Terminal/Stalled/Uncertain + decisions list. Linux probe reads `/proc/<pid>/stat` starttime (field after last ')' index 19) as BirthToken + `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` as BootID + sha256(hostname)[:16] as HostDigest (process_linux.go:16-45, process.go:47-51); darwin uses sysctl kinfo start time + kern.boottime (process_darwin.go); other platforms return partial identity + ErrProcessIdentityUnavailable (process_other.go:16-18). PID ≤ 0 rejected. `NewProcessOwner` mints a random `own_…` ID and self-probes, tolerating identity unavailability by keeping PID only (process.go:30-45). Expiry comparisons use SQLite's clock in production: `julianday(col) <= julianday('now', '-<grace> seconds')` vs bound parameters when a Clock is injected (tests only; sqlite.go:1132-1144). Clock-jump safety pinned by test (backward jump never expires early, forward jump reconciles).

### 2.9 Read paths
Snapshot (:594-606, loader :920-983) decodes one runs row with strict RFC3339Nano timestamps and correlation JSON (malformed → CodeCorrupt), then `Snapshot.Validate` (model.go:333-366: enums, UpdatedAt≥AcceptedAt, replay-boundary coherence oldest≤last+1, terminal↔finished↔lifecycle↔liveness consistency). Events (:809-854) pages ascending sequences after a cursor, limit default 200 max 512; payload/omission JSON decode failures are CodeCorrupt, not silently skipped. List (`lifecycle.go:196-266`) filters lifecycle/target/project/sprint/study with keyset cursor `(updated_at, run_id)` encoded as base64 JSON ≤1024 bytes, canonical RunID + parseable timestamp enforced (:278-291); each page row re-read as a full Snapshot. Health (:856-914) projects pragma facts, active/stalled/cancellation-uncertain counts, reconciliation backlog + oldest backlog age (same grace predicates), storage bytes vs quotas → status ok/degraded/failed with diagnostics, plus process-local metrics (metrics.go). ReconciliationEvidence (:532-572) exposes newest-first decisions with evidence collapsed to the two allowlisted classes or "omitted".

### 2.10 Command layer (`internal/app/run_commands.go`)
`runRepository` (:42-59) resolves the workspace, requires process-level runControlState, loads effective config, and fetches the per-process repository. Subcommands: list (:61-103), show (:105-129 — Snapshot rendered text or JSON), follow (:131-195 — poll Events 512-batch @250 ms when catching up else 1 s until `Lifecycle.IsTerminal() && after >= LastSequence`; ctx.Done returns nil, comment "Observation cancellation never changes the durable run"), cancel (:197-228 — canonical-reason whitelist, RequestCancellation, prints Changed flag), diagnostics (:230-276 — Health text/JSON + optional support export). Support export (:306-377) lists up to 50 runs, first 50 events each (sequence/type/omission only), ≤100 reconciliation evidence rows, ≤100 local log records; O_EXCL 0600 file, fsync, remove-on-failure, 1 MiB cap. Error mapping (:403-414): invalid_argument→ExitUsage, not_found→ExitValidation, conflict/terminal→ExitPartial, everything else→ExitRuntime.

### 2.11 Production writers (detail owned by surface `durable-operation-spine`)
- Process wiring: `runControlState` (app/run_control.go:23-95) caches one SQLiteRepository + LocalFileLogger + retention policy per workspace root for the process lifetime (policy drift rejected mid-process); first open runs startup Reconcile and fails closed on error; `Close()` closes pools LAST during shutdown. One Owner (`NewProcessOwner`) shared by all operations of the process.
- Runtime-backed runs: `controlledRuntime.StartRun` (run_control.go:159-343) Accept → Claim → build Fence → wrap OnEvent (content-hash coalescing of identical progress within ProgressCoalesceWindow=250 ms into Omission counts, :215-245) → control goroutine ticking 1 s: poll Snapshot, AcknowledgeCancellation+cancel on requested, Heartbeat every 5 s (HeartbeatInterval), Reconcile every 10 s; ANY persistence error cancels the run context and suppresses further display callbacks (:196-249) → trailing omission flush → normal terminal mapping (terminalOutcome :765-777) or persistence_degraded terminal proposed on a detached 30 s context (:322-331). Retries: append retried up to 5 s, terminal until success, only for ErrUnavailable|ErrBusy (:345-372).
- Interactive operations: `durableOperationManager.AcceptOperation` (durable_operations.go:97-138) Accept(alias=digest) with conflict resolution to Existing:true via ResolveOperationAlias; Claim; append lifecycle-running event (persistence-lost fallback terminal); store ownership in map + spawn control goroutine; operation context carries ParentRun + fence value. `RecordOperationEvent` (:158-221) coalesces and appends operation-scope events (cancel-on-error). `qaOwnershipFromContext` (:140-156) hands sprint a QAWriterToken{RunID,AttemptID,FencingGeneration} plus a heartbeat closure using `context.WithoutCancel`+30 s. `FinishOperation` (:266-300) flushes omissions, stops the control goroutine, maps state/error to outcome, proposes terminal. CLI verbs cross `beginDurableCLICommand` with EMPTY digest (inventory-pinned, app/run_control_inventory_test.go:12-46); TUI digests sha256(canonical+NUL+fingerprint) (tui/app.go:237-240); web passes the hub dedup key (web/operations.go:182).

## 3. Inputs / outputs

Inputs: workspace root path; wall clock via SQLite `julianday('now')` (production) or injected Clock (tests); caller-supplied Target/Correlation/Owner/ProcessIdentity/Fence/EventDraft/TerminalProposal values (validated+bounded); agentwrap/OpenCode runtime events filtered through app-side `runtimeEventDraft` before reaching Append; operator CLI args (run-id, reason, flags); `/proc` or sysctl process metadata during probes. Outputs: runs/attempts/events/operation_aliases/reconciliation_log rows in `.ultraplan/run-control.db` (+WAL/SHM files); `.ultraplan/run-control.log` JSON lines (local_log.go); Snapshot/Event/Page/Health/ReconcileReport structures consumed by CLI/web/TUI projections; typed errors (`Error{Code,Operation,RunID,Message,Retryable,Cause}`, errors.go:43-71); best-effort Notifier callbacks (unwired in production).

## 4. Authoritative state

- Database `.ultraplan/run-control.db` (DatabaseRelativePath, sqlite.go:22), schema v1 dual-recorded (`app_schema('run_control',1)` + PRAGMA user_version, :356-359):
  - `runs`: opaque run_id PK; target_kind/operation/project/sprint/study/stage/task; lifecycle 11-value CHECK incl. persistence_degraded (:245); liveness 7-value CHECK; record_state full/compacted/tombstone; timestamps; current_attempt_id FK→attempts; last_sequence/oldest_retained_sequence/history_complete/omission_total replay bookkeeping; correlation_json/product_status/confirmation_digest; cancellation quartet; terminal quintet with table-level CHECK tying terminal_outcome+finished_at+lifecycle (:268-269).
  - `attempts`: attempt_id PK; run FK CASCADE; ordinal>0 UNIQUE(run_id,ordinal); owner_id; fencing_generation>0 UNIQUE(run_id,fencing_generation); host_digest/boot_id/pid/process_birth_token birth identity; claimed/heartbeat/lease_expires timestamps; correlation_json; nullable outcome enum.
  - `events`: PK(run_id,sequence); committed_at; event_type 12-value CHECK; attempt FK; stage/task; payload_json; omission_json. Trigger `trg_events_immutable` RAISE(ABORT) on UPDATE (:327-331); deletes possible (compaction/retention/CASCADE).
  - `operation_aliases`: alias_id PK → run_id (CASCADE); alias_kind always 'operation' in practice; expires_at/recovery_code/recovery_guidance columns exist but are never written or read.
  - `reconciliation_log`: autoincrement id; run FK CASCADE; nullable attempt FK; observed_at; action/decision length-checked 1..128; evidence_json ≤16384.
  - Nine indexes listed at :333-341.
- Ancillary files under `.ultraplan/`: `run-control.log` (append-only JSON diagnostics, 1 MiB cap, 0600, symlink/regular-file contract enforced on open AND read, local_log.go:17,129); WAL/SHM sidecars counted toward quota; `<db>.migrate.lock` (migration surface).
- Shared file note: the SAME db file hosts a second package's tables (`product_states`/`product_state_items` via internal/productstate, separate pool, no version tracking — surface `product-state-mirror`; cross-package seam X1 in map-02).
- Retention policy from config (`run_control.full_history/tombstone_history/workspace_quota_bytes`) normalized to ≥1 h / ≥24 h ∧ ≥full / ≥64 MiB with 16 MiB reserved headroom (retention.go:13-33; defaults 7 d / 30 d / 512 MiB, model.go:422-429).

## 5. Invariants (as implemented)

- Identity grammar: RunID/AttemptID are `run_`/`att_` + 26 lowercase canonical base32 chars = exactly 128 bits (id.go:73-89); validated at every entry point; generated via crypto/rand.
- Single owner per run lifetime: claim requires `current_attempt_id IS NULL`; nothing ever clears it; late claims hit CodeConflict (live) or CodeTerminal (terminal).
- Fencing: every mutation by an owner goes through verifyFence (attempt row + owner + generation + runs.current_attempt_id agreement) plus per-statement CAS guards (last_sequence for Append/Ack/Cancel; terminal_outcome IS NULL everywhere; outcome IS NULL on heartbeat attempts-row update). Stale writers get typed CodeStaleFence, never silent success.
- Monotonic journal: sequences allocated as MAX+1 inside immediate transactions; immutability trigger blocks UPDATE; compaction only DELETEs non-authoritative types (progress/message/omission; tombstone adds accepted/claimed/lifecycle/recovery) and advances oldest_retained_sequence + history_complete=0 so readers can detect gaps.
- Single-winner terminal: one CAS-guarded transition; later proposers receive (incumbent, won=false); append-after-terminal CodeTerminal; request-cancellation-after-terminal idempotent no-op returning the winner; completion may win AFTER requested cancellation (test-pinned) leaving cancellation_state='requested' frozen beside a succeeded terminal.
- Active-state machine: validActiveTransition grammar; 'cancelling' absorbing among active states; terminal reachable only through the two arbitration paths.
- Cancellation request/acknowledge split: request is ownerless and idempotent; acknowledge is fenced; states none→requested→acknowledged ('uncertain' reserved/unwritten).
- Conservative liveness: stall (exact live identity + expired lease) never terminalizes; interrupted requires missing process or exact birth mismatch; anything unprovable → cleanup_uncertain; success is NEVER inferred by reconciliation.
- Quota/liveness coupling: soft gate pauses new accepts (retryable), hard gate blocks non-reserved appends and heartbeats while always permitting reserved recovery types (lifecycle/warning/cancellation/recovery/terminal/omission).
- Boundedness: target fields 512 B; safe values 32 KiB; correlations ≤256 KiB encoded; payloads ≤256 KiB; whole sanitized draft ≤128 KiB else replaced by a warning stub carrying omission metadata; per-run journal ≤4096 events/16 MiB; reconciliation evidence ≤16 KiB; log line ≤4 KiB/file ≤1 MiB; support export ≤1 MiB.
- Durability posture: WAL + synchronous FULL + immediate transactions on every mutation; busy_timeout 5 s; four pragmas verified at open; chmod-verified 0700/0600 private modes; symlink/non-regular rejection at directory, database, and log layers.
- Time authority: production expiry math executes inside SQLite so all processes share the database clock; injected clocks swap to parameter comparison (tests only — no production injector exists, map-02 X6).
- Typed error taxonomy with Retryable flags; SQLITE_BUSY/LOCKED→busy(retryable), PERM/READONLY→permission, CORRUPT/NOTADB→corrupt, FULL→quota(retryable), constraint(19)→typed conflicts; context errors pass through unwrapped (errors.go, classifyStoreError sqlite.go:1088-1111).

## 6. Trust boundaries

- Durable rows re-read as input: snapshots/events/evidence decode persisted JSON and timestamps strictly (malformed → CodeCorrupt surfaced to callers, sqlite.go:840,846,965); structural legality enforced by schema CHECKs plus post-load Snapshot.Validate. Anyone able to write the db file can rewrite gate inputs; controls are filesystem privacy (0700/0600, symlink rejection) + validation, not cryptographic integrity.
- Agent-derived event payloads pass TWO gates before storage: producer-side filtering in app (`runtimeEventDraft` run_control.go:417-545 — sensitive-key denylist secret/token/password/authorization/cookie/api_key/apikey/credential/auth, bounded values, one-level flattening, tool observation redaction replacing secret-shaped strings) and the storage-side sanitizer (`sanitizeEventDraft` sanitize.go:26-61 — allowlist of ~40 product field names, sensitive-fragment denylist secret/token/credential/password/prompt/payload/stdout/stderr/path/command, absolute/drive-letter paths and bearer/sk-/ghp_/github_pat_/private-key markers rejected, NUL/CR/LF stripped, oversize drafts replaced wholesale by a warning stub). Dropped detail becomes Omission counts, never silence.
- Structured logs apply the same sanitizer families locally (local_log.go:69-97: sensitive keys dropped, unsafe values "[omitted]", bounds enforced).
- Reconciliation evidence is deliberately reduced at WRITE time to a class string; the reader re-allowlists to two known values with "omitted" fallback (lifecycle.go:556-565).
- Pagination cursors are opaque bounded base64 JSON with canonical-ID and timestamp revalidation (lifecycle.go:278-291).
- Process identity from /proc or sysctl is treated as exact-birth proof only when complete; partial data classifies uncertain rather than dead (interfaces.go:17-20 contract comment).
- The local workspace is the trust domain: any local process with filesystem access to `.ultraplan/` can accept/claim/cancel/terminalize runs; there is no additional authorization layer between `run cancel` and the database.

## 7. External effects & lifecycle semantics

Effects confined to the workspace `.ultraplan/` tree and its own projections: row inserts/updates/deletes in one SQLite db (WAL sidecars), chmod enforcement, append-only log, migration lock file (other surface), best-effort wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)+incremental_vacuum after Compact (retention.go:151-152). No network, no signals to foreign processes (probes are read-only), no notifier wired.

Cancellation semantics: user/browser/TUI cancel persists `requested` (idempotent; changed=false on repeats or post-terminal); each owner control loop observes it within ≤1 tick, acknowledges (fenced), then cancels its own context; work drains through product-owned paths; terminal arbitration afterwards decides cancelled-vs-completed with single-winner guarantee. Shutdown: server drain writes leaseless cleanup-uncertain markers elsewhere; runcontrol terminals ride detached 30 s contexts so shutdown cannot prevent terminal commit (shutdown-ordering-chain seam).

Restart/crash semantics: abrupt owner death leaves running rows with expiring leases; startup Reconcile (every process open) plus periodic reconciles convert them to interrupted/cleanup_uncertain using birth-identity proof; unclaimed stale acceptances become interrupted after 45 s grace; repeated reconciliation is idempotent (process_integration_test.go:229-232). Restarted work is a NEW run (claim-once rule), correlated via Correlation.ProductRunID/ParentRun context, never adopted.

Retry/error semantics: busy/unavailable classified retryable; app spine retries appends ≤5 s and terminal proposals indefinitely-with-yields; quota failures stop acceptance/appends but reserve recovery-type writes; permission loss and closed pools produce typed failures with verified no-state-change (fault_test.go:87-129); SQLITE_FULL mid-append leaves last committed sequence intact (fault_test.go:12-50). Observation failures never mutate durable state (follow returns nil on ctx.Done; SSE handlers just stop streaming).

## 8. Immediate surface dependencies

- `durable-operation-spine` (internal/app run_control.go + durable_operations.go): sole production Claim/Append/Heartbeat/ProposeTerminal callers; mint-and-hand-off of fences (seam outer-inner-double-fencing; qa-writer-fence-handoff hands a fence-shaped token to sprint WITHOUT importing runcontrol).
- `shared-usecase-vocabulary`: three dedup-digest regimes (CLI empty / TUI hash / web session+token) converge on operation_aliases (seam three-acceptance-regimes-one-alias); RunUseCases DTO aliases (run_usecases.go).
- `run-cli-observation` + `web-operation-hub-sse`: consumers of Snapshot/Events/List/Health; duplicated poll/replay loop constants (seam observation-replay-parity); delivery gated on successful Append (seam persistence-gated-delivery); hub substitutes durable RunID for hub op id after AcceptOperation (web/operations.go:182-198).
- `product-state-mirror`: second pool on the same db file; independent pragma/migration posture (map-02 X1); storage.migrate command opens both pools simultaneously (storage_commands.go:60).
- `run-recovery-retention`: owns migrateSchema internals, Compact/backup/restore, retention aging — this surface calls into them at open (migrateSchema) and inline during Accept/Append (Compact, compactRunJournal).
- `config-inspection-health`: retention/quota knobs (runControlRetentionPolicy run_control.go:153-157).
- Sprint QA: consumes QAWriterToken fences and heartbeats the outer lease from inside sprint code (WithoutCancel+30 s).
- Platform: linux primary (probe via /proc), darwin variant, generic fallback reporting uncertainty; modernc.org/sqlite driver (go.mod v1.57.0); import boundary pinned to stdlib+driver only (import_boundary_test.go).

## 9. Contracts (CURRENT-CONTRACT evidence)

From ultraplan-workspace projects/ultraplan-go/docs/TRD.md §18C Phase 6 (~L2185-2212): durable envelope MUST include workspace-scoped run ID, target correlation, lifecycle timestamps, attempt/agentwrap/process correlations, owner identity + renewable lease + heartbeat + fencing value + safe process-birth identity, latest sequence + retention boundary, cancellation request/acknowledgement facts, ONE immutable arbitrated terminal result or explicit cleanup uncertainty. Acceptance atomic with run creation BEFORE child execution; persistence failure ⇒ child does not start. Events redacted before persistence, monotonic per-run sequences, committed before live fan-out; compaction must retain snapshot + lower replay boundary. Liveness conservative: "A PID alone is insufficient because of PID reuse"; reconciliation uses fencing or equivalent, records evidence and decisions, exposes stalled/interrupted/cleanup_uncertain where truth cannot be proven. Read visibility independent of originating session; cancellation idempotent, durably recorded, arbitrated so only one terminal wins.
TRD §20.1 (~L2330): serialize or fence competing lifecycle writers so stale owners cannot renew leases, append authoritative transitions, or overwrite the winning terminal outcome. TRD §20.2 (~L2356): cancellation from another supported process is FIRST persisted against the run, THEN routed to the current fenced owner; repetition safe; unreachable owner remains visibly pending/uncertain until reconciliation. §19.1/19.2: structured log/diagnostic fields include owner/fencing identity, lease state, reconciliation decisions, replay boundary; diagnostics must not include API keys/secrets. Sprint 35 requirements (workspace sprints/35-durable-run-observability/requirements.md L24, L40-41): startup and periodic reconciliation never infer success from process absence or artifact presence; exactly one terminal outcome wins across all races; repeated observers/cancellations cannot rewrite it. HISTORY note: TRD lists topology choices (coordinator vs fenced direct writers) as reasoning outputs; shipped choice is fenced direct multi-process repository access (sqlite.go:41-42 comment).

## 10. Tests (evidence map)

Package-internal (baseline green; coverage 68.7%, review/baseline/go-test-cover.txt:12):
- sqlite_test.go:17 schema/private-mode/index/foreign-key pinning incl. FK rejection of orphan events; :111 structured logs carry correlation fields and never leak payload values; :157 reopen persistence + integrity_check + immutability trigger blocks in-place event UPDATE; :197 symlink db rejected; :215 full happy-path accept→duplicate-conflict→claim(gen 1)→append(sequence/omission totals)→terminal win→loser-sees-incumbent→append-after-terminal CodeTerminal→event order; :287 two repositories × 20 goroutines allocate 40 gapless sequences (sorted assertion); :344 concurrent ProposeTerminal yields exactly one winner, observers agree on immutable outcome, exactly one terminal event; :398 blocked writer respects ctx deadline then succeeds after lock release.
- lifecycle_test.go:25 heartbeat liveness/idempotent double-request/ack + wrong-owner fence → ErrStaleFence on heartbeat and ack; :80 completion may win after cancellation; terminal cancel retry never rewrites winner; :102 all seven outcomes arbitrated through one path with immutable winners; :119 cancellation/terminal race preserves one winner + idempotent command; :176 reconcile decision matrix (live→stalled, missing→interrupted, birth-mismatch→interrupted, unsupported-probe→cleanup_uncertain) with evidence allowlist check and "never succeeded" assertion; :233 clock-jump safety (backward jump no early expiry; forward jump reconciles); :261 unclaimed acceptance backlog health accounting + grace terminalization + late-claim CodeTerminal + acceptance_timestamp_only evidence; :313 native probe matches NewProcessOwner exactly (skips when platform lacks birth identity).
- sanitize_test.go:10 hostile payload fields dropped with omission count 4 and no secret/path leakage; :38 nine oversize allowed fields collapse to warning stub `event_detail_oversize`.
- fault_test.go:12 PRAGMA max_page_count exhaustion → typed ErrQuota with no uncommitted append success (snapshot == last committed); :52 closed repository fails all six mutations typed Unavailable/Busy; :87 query_only mode → typed ErrPermission on all five mutations with before==after snapshot.
- process_integration_test.go:15 two real subprocesses share one durable sequence (40 gapless events); :83 cross-process cancellation persisted and observed; :127 unclaimed acceptance from an exited process reconciled after grace; :177 claimed owner exit → interrupted after lease+grace, second reconcile no-op; helper drives accept/accept-claim/cancel/append modes via env.
- id_test.go uniqueness/canonicalization/rejection classes; model_test.go snapshot-validation invariant table; local_log_test/sanitize_test cover log sanitizer paths; import_boundary_test.go pins dependency allowlist.
App-level: durable_operations_test.go (accept/claim/record/finish flows incl. second-manager conflict), run_commands_test.go (show/cancel JSON envelopes; claimed fixture), run_control_inventory_test.go (every runtime-backed CLI entry crosses beginDurableCLICommand — counts pinned per file), web run_handlers_test.go (multi-repo claim conflict, cancel, SSE replay shapes).
Baseline: full go test / -race / vet green at frozen SHA (review/baseline/summary.json).

Coverage gaps noted factually: no test exercises Claim racing a concurrent Claim on one run at process level (conflict branch covered only sequentially); reconcile batch-limit interaction (unclaimed budget starving expired-owner scan) untested; operation_aliases expires_at/recovery_code paths have no tests or code; no test for Health degraded/failed status transitions; no test covers Append when compaction exhausts removable types.

## 11. Explicit unknowns / open questions (for later reviewers)

1. Event types `accepted`/`claimed` are schema-valid and tombstone-compaction targets but NO production or test path ever writes them; intent (reserved vs vestigial) undocumented — affects anyone reconstructing history from events alone.
2. `operation_aliases.expires_at/recovery_code/recovery_guidance` are never written or read anywhere; alias rows live exactly as long as their run (CASCADE). Whether expiry/recovery was deferred deliberately is unstated.
3. Claim-once semantics: because current_attempt_id is never cleared, a run can never be re-claimed after its owner dies — recovery is always a NEW run. No doc statement found making this permanence explicit.
4. Pragma verification covers four of six DSN settings; `_txlock=immediate` and `_defensive=1` are set but never read back (map-02 SA-1). Correctness of the MAX+1 allocation strategy depends on immediate transactions being effective for every connection.
5. Reconcile spends its batch budget on unclaimed runs first; under a large ownerless backlog the expired-owner scan gets only the remainder — starvation shape unstated.
6. recordReconciliation errors are ignored at both call sites (`_ =`), so decisions can be applied without durable evidence rows.
7. The reconciler terminalizes using the dead attempt's own fence; safety rests on the claim-once invariant (#3) — if ownership were ever transferable, this fence reuse would need revisit.
8. Hard-quota heartbeat refusal forces lease expiry as the shutdown signal for healthy owners; interplay with long-running product operations that ignore context until the next tick (≤1 s + operation duration) is timing-dependent.
9. `cancellation_state='uncertain'` is readable/countable but unreachable through any writer; who would set it and when is unspecified.
10. storageBytes counts every `run-control.db*` regular file (including .migrate.lock and backups) toward quota — intentional? undocumented.
11. compactRunJournal runs synchronously inside every Append transaction once limits are exceeded (latency coupling); a run saturated exclusively with non-removable event types makes ALL further appends fail permanently with CodeQuota until manual intervention — recovery story unstated.
12. Windows has no probe implementation (generic fallback reports uncertainty); platform support matrix implicit (linux-first, darwin variant present).
13. List issues one Snapshot query per row (N+1 within page limit ≤200); performance envelope for large workspaces undocumented.
14. `run follow`/SSE/hub replay loops duplicate cadence constants independently (observation-replay-parity seam); parity relies on copy-paste, unpinned by any shared test.

— End of context pack. Descriptive only; no defect claims made or implied.

# Context Pack: `run-journal-fencing` — Run-control SQLite journal and fencing

Target: ultraplan-go @ 8eef70f4903b25580719960009a170945bdad9ad (frozen; working tree differs only in internal/sprint smoke files, runcontrol+app identical).
Planning context: ultraplan-workspace @ ab12dc38059c9bf485f9aced9075bcd7d924cac5.
Domain: durability-core. Risk: critical. Descriptive only — no defect judgments.

## 1. Purpose

`internal/runcontrol` is the durable identity and arbitration layer for every executing UltraPlan operation (doc.go:1-6). It records: the accepted execution (`runs`), at most one fenced owner attempt per run (`attempts`), a strictly ordered append-only sanitized event journal (`events`), optional operation alias identities for dedup (`operation_aliases`), and reconciliation decision evidence (`reconciliation_log`) — all in one private SQLite database at `.ultraplan/run-control.db`. It deliberately does NOT own product workflow state, artifacts, or runtime supervision (doc.go, interfaces.go:47-48). Core mechanisms: accept-before-execute; fenced claim with lease + heartbeat; cancellation request/acknowledge split across processes; single-winner terminal compare-and-set over seven outcomes including explicit uncertainty (`cleanup_uncertain`, `persistence_degraded`); conservative birth-identity reconciliation that never infers success.

## 2. Entrypoints and control flow

### 2.1 Open path (`sqlite.go:60-134`)
`OpenSQLite(ctx, workspaceRoot, SQLiteOptions)`: validate workspace root (abs, dir, sqlite.go:136-152) → prepare private storage (`preparePrivateDatabase`, :154-191): `.ultraplan/` created 0700, symlink/non-dir rejected via Lstat (:159-165); `run-control.db` created `O_CREATE|O_EXCL|O_RDWR` 0600, symlink/non-regular rejected (:172-186); `enforcePrivateMode` chmods then re-stats to verify exact mode (:193-205) → open DSN with fixed pragmas `_busy_timeout=5000 _foreign_keys=on _journal_mode=WAL _synchronous=FULL _txlock=immediate _defensive=1` (:73-80) → ping, then `verifyPragmas` reads back journal_mode/synchronous/foreign_keys/busy_timeout only (:207-227) → `migrateSchema` (migration.go:25-82; current-version DBs take the lock-free verify path — schema record equality + integrity check; migration itself belongs to surface `run-recovery-retention`) → connection pool default 4, operator-cappable 1..16 (:92-100) → repository assembled with injected-or-wall Clock, RandomIDSource, normalized retention policy (:107-131).

### 2.2 Accept (`sqlite.go:378-470`)
Quota gates first: `storageBytes()` sums sizes of all regular files whose names start with `run-control.db` in `.ultraplan/` (retention.go:35-56 — includes `-wal`/`-shm`/`.migrate.lock`/backups); usage ≥ 80% of hard quota triggers inline `Compact(ctx,64)` (:384-390); usage ≥ soft quota (hard − 16 MiB headroom) refuses acceptance with retryable `CodeQuota` (:391-395). Then Target/Correlation validation, ProductStatus/ConfirmationDigest ≤ MaxSafeValueBytes (:396-404), RunID minted when absent and validated (:405-415), correlation marshaled bounded to 256 KiB (:416). One immediate transaction inserts the `runs` row (lifecycle `accepted`, liveness `unknown`, record_state `full`, cancellation_state `none`, last_sequence 0) (:429-444); duplicate RunID → typed Conflict (:440-442). Optional OperationAlias inserts an `operation_aliases` row in the same tx; alias conflict → Conflict (:445-455). Snapshot loaded + validated inside the tx before commit (:456-462). NOTE: Accept writes NO event row; the journal stays empty until the first cancellation/append/terminal/reconcile write.

### 2.3 Claim (`sqlite.go:486-592`)
Validates RunID/Owner/Correlation/Lease>0 and AttemptID (minted when absent) (:490-512). In one immediate transaction: read lifecycle+current_attempt (:529); terminal run → `CodeTerminal`; existing current attempt → `CodeConflict` "run already has a current owner attempt" (:533-538). Next lifecycle = running, preserved as cancelling if already cancelling (:539-542). Ordinal = MAX(ordinal)+1 and fencing_generation = MAX(fencing_generation)+1 over the run's attempts (:543-546); attempts table enforces `UNIQUE(run_id,ordinal)` and `UNIQUE(run_id,fencing_generation)` (:288-289) plus `fencing_generation > 0` (:278). INSERT attempt (owner_id, host_digest, boot_id, pid, process_birth_token, claimed_at=heartbeat_at=now, lease_expires_at=now+lease) (:547-560), then CAS-style UPDATE of runs: `SET current_attempt_id=?, lifecycle=?, liveness='live', started_at=COALESCE(started_at,?), updated_at=? WHERE run_id=? AND current_attempt_id IS NULL AND terminal_outcome IS NULL`; RowsAffected ≠ 1 → Conflict (:561-571). Snapshot validated pre-commit. Because no code path ever nulls `current_attempt_id`, each run is claimed AT MOST once in its lifetime (grep over package: only setter is sqlite.go:563; reconcile paths require it NULL/non-terminal).

INSERT attempt (owner_id, host_digest, boot_id, pid, process_birth_token, claimed_at=heartbeat_at=now, lease_expires_at=now+lease) (:547-560), then CAS-style UPDATE of runs: `SET current_attempt_id=?, lifecycle=?, liveness='live', started_at=COALESCE(started_at,?), updated_at=? WHERE run_id=? AND current_attempt_id IS NULL AND terminal_outcome IS NULL`; RowsAffected ≠ 1 → Conflict (:561-571). Snapshot validated pre-commit. Because no code path ever nulls `current_attempt_id`, each run is claimed AT MOST once in its lifetime (grep over package: only setter is sqlite.go:563; reconcile paths require it NULL/non-terminal).

22: ### 2.4 Append (`sqlite.go:608-711`)
23: Fence validated (RunID+AttemptID grammar, OwnerID non-empty, generation > 0; model.go:287-298) → draft normalized (typed fields copied into payload, model.go:490-505) and sanitized (§6) → hard-quota gate: usage ≥ hard quota rejects all event types except reserved ones (lifecycle/warning/cancellation/recovery/terminal/omission, :618-622, :713-720) → draft validation (:1005-1029: known type/scope, active-only lifecycle hint, stage/task ≤512 bytes without NUL/CR/LF, payload keys ≤128 bytes/values ≤32 KiB without NUL, omission needs positive count). Immediate transaction: `verifyFence` (:985-1003 — attempt row must exist for (run_id, attempt_id), owner_id and fencing_generation must match, and runs.current_attempt_id must equal the fence's attempt) → read last_sequence+lifecycle; terminal run → `CodeTerminal` immutable (:652-658); lifecycle hint must satisfy `validActiveTransition` (:1031-1047: accepted→{queued,running,cancelling}, queued→{running,cancelling}, running→cancelling, cancelling→nothing, self-transitions allowed) → sequence = last_sequence+1 inserted into events (:666-672) → CAS UPDATE runs: `SET last_sequence=?, lifecycle=?, omission_total += ?, updated_at=? WHERE run_id=? AND last_sequence=? AND current_attempt_id=? AND terminal_outcome IS NULL`; RowsAffected ≠ 1 → `CodeStaleFence` "event writer lost its authoritative fence" (:677-686) → inline `compactRunJournal` when the run exceeds 4096 events or 16 MiB retained payload bytes: deletes oldest progress/message/omission events (never the just-written sequence), sets record_state=compacted, history_complete=0, oldest_retained_sequence=MIN(sequence) or last+1; nothing removable → typed `CodeQuota` failure (retention.go:58-95) → snapshot validated, commit, notify (no-op unless Notifier wired; production wires none), debug log.

25: ### 2.5 Heartbeat (`lifecycle.go:14-68`)

Immediate transaction: verifyFence → CAS UPDATE attempts `SET heartbeat_at=?, lease_expires_at=now+lease WHERE ... AND outcome IS NULL` (RowsAffected≠1 → StaleFence) → CAS UPDATE runs liveness='live' where current attempt matches and not terminal (RowsAffected≠1 → StaleFence) → snapshot, commit, metric. 28: ### 2.6 Cancellation request / acknowledge split
29: - RequestCancellation (`lifecycle.go:70-134`): reason trimmed, must be non-empty, ≤32 KiB, no NUL/CR/LF (:77-80); CLI additionally whitelists {user_requested, operator_requested, shutdown_requested, quota_exceeded} (run_commands.go:394-401). No fence required — works ownerless. Idempotent short-circuit: already terminal OR any non-none cancellation state returns (current snapshot, changed=false) after committing the read tx (:91-96). Otherwise inserts a `cancellation` event (attempt_id nullable — set only when a current attempt exists, :102-109) and CAS UPDATEs runs: `SET lifecycle='cancelling', cancellation_state='requested', reason, requested_at, updated_at, last_sequence=? WHERE run_id=? AND terminal_outcome IS NULL AND cancellation_state='none' AND last_sequence=?` (:110-120); lost race → retryable Conflict.
30: - AcknowledgeCancellation (`lifecycle.go:136-194`): fence-gated. Short-circuits (changed=false) when terminal or already acknowledged; state ≠ requested → Conflict; else inserts an ack `cancellation` event and CAS UPDATEs `cancellation_state='acknowledged', acknowledged_at` guarded by current_attempt match + state=requested + unchanged last_sequence (:156-181).
31: - `cancellation_state='uncertain'` exists in the schema enum and Health projection but no code path writes it (grep: only model.go definition + Health count sqlite.go:877).

33: ### 2.7 ProposeTerminal (`sqlite.go:722-807`)
34: The ONLY writer of terminal state (plus reconcileUnclaimed below). Validated proposal (outcome ∈ closed 7-value enum, reason/proposer bounded, :731-736). Immediate transaction: verifyFence → loadSnapshot; if Terminal already present, COMMIT the read tx and return (winner, won=false, nil) — losers observe the incumbent outcome instead of erroring (:753-758). Winner path: insert one `terminal` event at last_sequence+1 (payload {outcome,reason}) (:759-768), then CAS UPDATE runs setting lifecycle=outcome.Lifecycle(), liveness='terminal', finished_at, last_sequence, terminal_* columns `WHERE run_id=? AND current_attempt_id=? AND terminal_outcome IS NULL`; RowsAffected ≠ 1 → StaleFence loser (:769-786); attempts.outcome stamped on the winner's own attempt (:787-790); snapshot validated against the full terminal-consistency rules (model.go:355-364) before commit. Schema CHECK ties terminal_outcome ↔ finished_at ↔ terminal lifecycle (:268-269).

36: ### 2.8 Reconcile (`lifecycle.go:301-416`)
37: Runs on every repository open (app/run_control.go:66) and every 10 s inside active-operation control loops. Grace defaults to ReconciliationGrace=45 s; batch default 64/max 256. Pass 1 — unclaimed runs (`current_attempt_id IS NULL AND accepted_at older than grace`, :320-339): `reconcileUnclaimed` (:427-479) re-checks state in-tx, inserts one `terminal` event (attempt_id NULL) and CAS-terminalizes to interrupted/"owner_never_claimed_after_grace" guarded by `current_attempt_id IS NULL AND terminal_outcome IS NULL`; concurrent claim/win → silent no-op. Pass 2 — expired owners (runs joined to their current attempt where lease_expires_at older than grace, :360-383): probe recorded PID via ProcessProbe; `reconcileProcessDecision` matrix (:481-495):
38: - ErrProcessNotFound → interrupted, "owner_process_missing_after_grace";
39: - other probe error → cleanup_uncertain, "owner_process_identity_uncertain_after_grace";
40: - incomplete stored OR observed identity fields → cleanup_uncertain;
41: - exact field mismatch (host/boot/pid/birth) → interrupted, "owner_process_birth_mismatch_after_grace";
42: - exact live match → NO terminal: markStalled only (:497-509, liveness='stalled' CAS on still-current attempt; StaleFence tolerated).
43: Terminal proposals ride the DEAD attempt's own recorded fence (ProposedBy="reconciler"); ErrTerminal/ErrStaleFence from racing writers are tolerated (:392, :401). Every decision appended to reconciliation_log via recordReconciliation (:511-527; evidence reduced to class strings safe_identity_only / acceptance_timestamp_only; errors deliberately ignored by callers `_ = r.recordReconciliation(...)` :352, :411). Report counters Scanned/Terminal/Stalled/Uncertain + decisions list. Linux probe reads `/proc/<pid>/stat` starttime (field after last ')' index 19) as BirthToken + `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` as BootID + sha256(hostname)[:16] as HostDigest (process_linux.go:16-45, process.go:47-51); darwin uses sysctl kinfo start time + kern.boottime (process_darwin.go); other platforms return partial identity + ErrProcessIdentityUnavailable (process_other.go:16-18). PID ≤ 0 rejected. `NewProcessOwner` mints a random `own_…` ID and self-probes, tolerating identity unavailability by keeping PID only (process.go:30-45). Expiry comparisons use SQLite's clock in production: `julianday(col) <= julianday('now', '-<grace> seconds')` vs bound parameters when a Clock is injected (tests only; sqlite.go:1132-1144). Clock-jump safety pinned by test (backward jump never expires early, forward jump reconciles).

73: ## 5. Invariants (as implemented)
74: 
75: - Identity grammar: RunID/AttemptID are `run_`/`att_` + 26 lowercase canonical base32 chars = exactly 128 bits (id.go:73-89); validated at every entry point; generated via crypto/rand.
76: - Single owner per run lifetime: claim requires `current_attempt_id IS NULL`; nothing ever clears it; late claims hit CodeConflict (live) or CodeTerminal (terminal).
77: - Fencing: every mutation by an owner goes through verifyFence (attempt row + owner + generation + runs.current_attempt_id agreement) plus per-statement CAS guards (last_sequence for Append/Ack/Cancel; terminal_outcome IS NULL everywhere; outcome IS NULL on heartbeat attempts-row update). Stale writers get typed CodeStaleFence, never silent success.
78: - Monotonic journal: sequences allocated as MAX+1 inside immediate transactions; immutability trigger blocks UPDATE; compaction only DELETEs non-authoritative types (progress/message/omission; tombstone adds accepted/claimed/lifecycle/recovery) and advances oldest_retained_sequence + history_complete=0 so readers can detect gaps.
79: - Single-winner terminal: one CAS-guarded transition; later proposers receive (incumbent, won=false); append-after-terminal CodeTerminal; request-cancellation-after-terminal idempotent no-op returning the winner; completion may win AFTER requested cancellation (test-pinned) leaving cancellation_state='requested' frozen beside a succeeded terminal.
80: - Active-state machine: validActiveTransition grammar; 'cancelling' absorbing among active states; terminal reachable only through the two arbitration paths.
81: - Cancellation request/acknowledge split: request is ownerless and idempotent; acknowledge is fenced; states none→requested→acknowledged ('uncertain' reserved/unwritten).
82: - Conservative liveness: stall (exact live identity + expired lease) never terminalizes; interrupted requires missing process or exact birth mismatch; anything unprovable → cleanup_uncertain; success is NEVER inferred by reconciliation.
83: - Quota/liveness coupling: soft gate pauses new accepts (retryable), hard gate blocks non-reserved appends and heartbeats while always permitting reserved recovery types (lifecycle/warning/cancellation/recovery/terminal/omission).
84: - Boundedness: target fields 512 B; safe values 32 KiB; correlations ≤256 KiB encoded; payloads ≤256 KiB; whole sanitized draft ≤128 KiB else replaced by a warning stub carrying omission metadata; per-run journal ≤4096 events/16 MiB; reconciliation evidence ≤16 KiB; log line ≤4 KiB/file ≤1 MiB; support export ≤1 MiB.
85: - Durability posture: WAL + synchronous FULL + immediate transactions on every mutation; busy_timeout 5 s; four pragmas verified at open; chmod-verified 0700/0600 private modes; symlink/non-regular rejection at directory, database, and log layers.
86: - Time authority: production expiry math executes inside SQLite so all processes share the database clock; injected clocks swap to parameter comparison (tests only — no production injector exists, map-02 X6).
87: - Typed error taxonomy with Retryable flags; SQLITE_BUSY/LOCKED→busy(retryable), PERM/READONLY→permission, CORRUPT/NOTADB→corrupt, FULL→quota(retryable), constraint(19)→typed conflicts; context errors pass through unwrapped (errors.go, classifyStoreError sqlite.go:1088-1111).
88: 
89: ## 6. Trust boundaries
90: 
91: - Durable rows re-read as input: snapshots/events/evidence decode persisted JSON and timestamps strictly (malformed → CodeCorrupt surfaced to callers, sqlite.go:840,846,965); structural legality enforced by schema CHECKs plus post-load Snapshot.Validate. Anyone able to write the db file can rewrite gate inputs; controls are filesystem privacy (0700/0600, symlink rejection) + validation, not cryptographic integrity.
92: - Agent-derived event payloads pass TWO gates before storage: producer-side filtering in app (`runtimeEventDraft` run_control.go:417-545 — sensitive-key denylist secret/token/password/authorization/cookie/api_key/apikey/credential/auth, bounded values, one-level flattening, tool observation redaction replacing secret-shaped strings) and the storage-side sanitizer (`sanitizeEventDraft` sanitize.go:26-61 — allowlist of ~40 product field names, sensitive-fragment denylist secret/token/credential/password/prompt/payload/stdout/stderr/path/command, absolute/drive-letter paths and bearer/sk-/ghp_/github_pat_/private-key markers rejected, NUL/CR/LF stripped, oversize drafts replaced wholesale by a warning stub). Dropped detail becomes Omission counts, never silence.
93: - Structured logs apply the same sanitizer families locally (local_log.go:69-97: sensitive keys dropped, unsafe values "[omitted]", bounds enforced).
94: - Reconciliation evidence is deliberately reduced at WRITE time to a class string; the reader re-allowlists to two known values with "omitted" fallback (lifecycle.go:556-565).
95: - Pagination cursors are opaque bounded base64 JSON with canonical-ID and timestamp revalidation (lifecycle.go:278-291).
96: - Process identity from /proc or sysctl is treated as exact-birth proof only when complete; partial data classifies uncertain rather than dead (interfaces.go:17-20 contract comment).
97: - The local workspace is the trust domain: any local process with filesystem access to `.ultraplan/` can accept/claim/cancel/terminalize runs; there is no additional authorization layer between `run cancel` and the database.

99: ## 7. External effects & lifecycle semantics
100: 
101: Effects confined to the workspace `.ultraplan/` tree and its own projections: row inserts/updates/deletes in one SQLite db (WAL sidecars), chmod enforcement, append-only log, migration lock file (other surface), best-effort wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)+incremental_vacuum after Compact (retention.go:151-152). No network, no signals to foreign processes (probes are read-only), no notifier wired.
102: 
103: Cancellation semantics: user/browser/TUI cancel persists `requested` (idempotent; changed=false on repeats or post-terminal); each owner control loop observes it within ≤1 tick, acknowledges (fenced), then cancels its own context; work drains through product-owned paths; terminal arbitration afterwards decides cancelled-vs-completed with single-winner guarantee. Shutdown: server drain writes leaseless cleanup-uncertain markers elsewhere; runcontrol terminals ride detached 30 s contexts so shutdown cannot prevent terminal commit (shutdown-ordering-chain seam).
104: 
105: Restart/crash semantics: abrupt owner death leaves running rows with expiring leases; startup Reconcile (every process open) plus periodic reconciles convert them to interrupted/cleanup_uncertain using birth-identity proof; unclaimed stale acceptances become interrupted after 45 s grace; repeated reconciliation is idempotent (process_integration_test.go:229-232). Restarted work is a NEW run (claim-once rule), correlated via Correlation.ProductRunID/ParentRun context, never adopted.
106: 
107: Retry/error semantics: busy/unavailable classified retryable; app spine retries appends ≤5 s and terminal proposals indefinitely-with-yields; quota failures stop acceptance/appends but reserve recovery-type writes; permission loss and closed pools produce typed failures with verified no-state-change (fault_test.go:87-129); SQLITE_FULL mid-append leaves last committed sequence intact (fault_test.go:12-50). Observation failures never mutate durable state (follow returns nil on ctx.Done; SSE handlers just stop streaming).

120: ## 9. Contracts (CURRENT-CONTRACT evidence)
121: 
122: From ultraplan-workspace projects/ultraplan-go/docs/TRD.md §18C Phase 6 (~L2185-2212): durable envelope MUST include workspace-scoped run ID, target correlation, lifecycle timestamps, attempt/agentwrap/process correlations, owner identity + renewable lease + heartbeat + fencing value + safe process-birth identity, latest sequence + retention boundary, cancellation request/acknowledgement facts, ONE immutable arbitrated terminal result or explicit cleanup uncertainty. Acceptance atomic with run creation BEFORE child execution; persistence failure ⇒ child does not start. Events redacted before persistence, monotonic per-run sequences, committed before live fan-out; compaction must retain snapshot + lower replay boundary. Liveness conservative: "A PID alone is insufficient because of PID reuse"; reconciliation uses fencing or equivalent, records evidence and decisions, exposes stalled/interrupted/cleanup_uncertain where truth cannot be proven. Read visibility independent of originating session; cancellation idempotent, durably recorded, arbitrated so only one terminal wins.
123: TRD §20.1 (~L2330): serialize or fence competing lifecycle writers so stale owners cannot renew leases, append authoritative transitions, or overwrite the winning terminal outcome. TRD §20.2 (~L2356): cancellation from another supported process is FIRST persisted against the run, THEN routed to the current fenced owner; repetition safe; unreachable owner remains visibly pending/uncertain until reconciliation. §19.1/19.2: structured log/diagnostic fields include owner/fencing identity, lease state, reconciliation decisions, replay boundary; diagnostics must not include API keys/secrets. Sprint 35 requirements (workspace sprints/35-durable-run-observability/requirements.md L24, L40-41): startup and periodic reconciliation never infer success from process absence or artifact presence; exactly one terminal outcome wins across all races; repeated observers/cancellations cannot rewrite it. HISTORY note: TRD lists topology choices (coordinator vs fenced direct writers) as reasoning outputs; shipped choice is fenced direct multi-process repository access (sqlite.go:41-42 comment).

5: Domain: durability-core. Risk: critical. Descriptive only — no defect judgments.
6: 
7: ## 1. Purpose
8: 
9: `internal/runcontrol` is the durable identity and arbitration layer for every executing UltraPlan operation (doc.go:1-6). It records: the accepted execution (`runs`), at most one fenced owner attempt per run (`attempts`), a strictly ordered append-only sanitized event journal (`events`), optional operation alias identities for dedup (`operation_aliases`), and reconciliation decision evidence (`reconciliation_log`) — all in one private SQLite database at `.ultraplan/run-control.db`. It deliberately does NOT own product workflow state, artifacts, or runtime supervision (doc.go, interfaces.go:47-48). Core mechanisms: accept-before-execute; fenced claim with lease + heartbeat; cancellation request/acknowledge split across processes; single-winner terminal compare-and-set over seven outcomes including explicit uncertainty (`cleanup_uncertain`, `persistence_degraded`); conservative birth-identity reconciliation that never infers success.
10: 
11: ## 2. Entrypoints and control flow
12: 
13: ### 2.1 Open path (`sqlite.go:60-134`)
14: `OpenSQLite(ctx, workspaceRoot, SQLiteOptions)`: validate workspace root (abs, dir, sqlite.go:136-152) → prepare private storage (`preparePrivateDatabase`, :154-191): `.ultraplan/` created 0700, symlink/non-dir rejected via Lstat (:159-165); `run-control.db` created `O_CREATE|O_EXCL|O_RDWR` 0600, symlink/non-regular rejected (:172-186); `enforcePrivateMode` chmods then re-stats to verify exact mode (:193-205) → open DSN with fixed pragmas `_busy_timeout=5000 _foreign_keys=on _journal_mode=WAL _synchronous=FULL _txlock=immediate _defensive=1` (:73-80) → ping, then `verifyPragmas` reads back journal_mode/synchronous/foreign_keys/busy_timeout only (:207-227) → `migrateSchema` (migration.go:25-82; current-version DBs take the lock-free verify path — schema record equality + integrity check; migration itself belongs to surface `run-recovery-retention`) → connection pool default 4, operator-cappable 1..16 (:92-100) → repository assembled with injected-or-wall Clock, RandomIDSource, normalized retention policy (:107-131).
15: 
16: ### 2.2 Accept (`sqlite.go:378-470`)
17: Quota gates first: `storageBytes()` sums sizes of all regular files whose names start with `run-control.db` in `.ultraplan/` (retention.go:35-56 — includes `-wal`/`-shm`/`.migrate.lock`/backups); usage ≥ 80% of hard quota triggers inline `Compact(ctx,64)` (:384-390); usage ≥ soft quota (hard − 16 MiB headroom) refuses acceptance with retryable `CodeQuota` (:391-395). Then Target/Correlation validation, ProductStatus/ConfirmationDigest ≤ MaxSafeValueBytes (:396-404), RunID minted when absent and validated (:405-415), correlation marshaled bounded to 256 KiB (:416). One immediate transaction inserts the `runs` row (lifecycle `accepted`, liveness `unknown`, record_state `full`, cancellation_state `none`, last_sequence 0) (:429-444); duplicate RunID → typed Conflict (:440-442). Optional OperationAlias inserts an `operation_aliases` row in the same tx; alias conflict → Conflict (:445-455). Snapshot loaded + validated inside the tx before commit (:456-462). NOTE: Accept writes NO event row; the journal stays empty until the first cancellation/append/terminal/reconcile write.
18: 
19: ### 2.3 Claim (`sqlite.go:486-592`)
20: Validates RunID/Owner/Correlation/Lease>0 and AttemptID (minted when absent) (:490-512). In one immediate transaction: read lifecycle+current_attempt (:529); terminal run → `CodeTerminal`; existing current attempt → `CodeConflict` "run already has a current owner attempt" (:533-538). Next lifecycle = running, preserved as cancelling if already cancelling (:539-542). Ordinal = MAX(ordinal)+1 and fencing_generation = MAX(fencing_generation)+1 over the run's attempts (:543-546); attempts table enforces `UNIQUE(run_id,ordinal)` and `UNIQUE(run_id,fencing_generation)` (:288-289) plus `fencing_generation > 0` (:278). INSERT attempt (owner_id, host_digest, boot_id, pid, process_birth_token, claimed_at=heartbeat_at=now, lease_expires_at=now+lease) (:547-560), then CAS-style UPDATE of runs: `SET current_attempt_id=?, lifecycle=?, liveness='live', started_at=COALESCE(started_at,?), updated_at=? WHERE run_id=? AND current_attempt_id IS NULL AND terminal_outcome IS NULL`; RowsAffected ≠ 1 → Conflict (:561-571). Snapshot validated pre-commit. Because no code path ever nulls `current_attempt_id`, each run is claimed AT MOST once in its lifetime (grep over package: only setter is sqlite.go:563; reconcile paths require it NULL/non-terminal).
21: 
22: ### 2.4 Append (`sqlite.go:608-711`)
23: Fence validated (RunID+AttemptID grammar, OwnerID non-empty, generation > 0; model.go:287-298) → draft normalized (typed fields copied into payload, model.go:490-505) and sanitized (§6) → hard-quota gate: usage ≥ hard quota rejects all event types except reserved ones (lifecycle/warning/cancellation/recovery/terminal/omission, :618-622, :713-720) → draft validation (:1005-1029: known type/scope, active-only lifecycle hint, stage/task ≤512 bytes without NUL/CR/LF, payload keys ≤128 bytes/values ≤32 KiB without NUL, omission needs positive count). Immediate transaction: `verifyFence` (:985-1003 — attempt row must exist for (run_id, attempt_id), owner_id and fencing_generation must match, and runs.current_attempt_id must equal the fence's attempt) → read last_sequence+lifecycle; terminal run → `CodeTerminal` immutable (:652-658); lifecycle hint must satisfy `validActiveTransition` (:1031-1047: accepted→{queued,running,cancelling}, queued→{running,cancelling}, running→cancelling, cancelling→nothing, self-transitions allowed) → sequence = last_sequence+1 inserted into events (:666-672) → CAS UPDATE runs: `SET last_sequence=?, lifecycle=?, omission_total += ?, updated_at=? WHERE run_id=? AND last_sequence=? AND current_attempt_id=? AND terminal_outcome IS NULL`; RowsAffected ≠ 1 → `CodeStaleFence` "event writer lost its authoritative fence" (:677-686) → inline `compactRunJournal` when the run exceeds 4096 events or 16 MiB retained payload bytes: deletes oldest progress/message/omission events (never the just-written sequence), sets record_state=compacted, history_complete=0, oldest_retained_sequence=MIN(sequence) or last+1; nothing removable → typed `CodeQuota` failure (retention.go:58-95) → snapshot validated, commit, notify (no-op unless Notifier wired; production wires none), debug log.
24: 
25: ### 2.5 Heartbeat (`lifecycle.go:14-68`)
26: Lease > 0 required; hard-quota gate REFUSES heartbeats at ≥ hard quota ("hard quota requires the owner to stop active work", :24-28). Immediate transaction: verifyFence → CAS UPDATE attempts `SET heartbeat_at=?, lease_expires_at=now+lease WHERE ... AND outcome IS NULL` (RowsAffected≠1 → StaleFence) → CAS UPDATE runs liveness='live' where current attempt matches and not terminal (RowsAffected≠1 → StaleFence) → snapshot, commit, metric. Heartbeat both extends the lease and clears a prior `stalled` marking.
27: 
28: ### 2.6 Cancellation request / acknowledge split
29: - RequestCancellation (`lifecycle.go:70-134`): reason trimmed, must be non-empty, ≤32 KiB, no NUL/CR/LF (:77-80); CLI additionally whitelists {user_requested, operator_requested, shutdown_requested, quota_exceeded} (run_commands.go:394-401). No fence required — works ownerless. Idempotent short-circuit: already terminal OR any non-none cancellation state returns (current snapshot, changed=false) after committing the read tx (:91-96). Otherwise inserts a `cancellation` event (attempt_id nullable — set only when a current attempt exists, :102-109) and CAS UPDATEs runs: `SET lifecycle='cancelling', cancellation_state='requested', reason, requested_at, updated_at, last_sequence=? WHERE run_id=? AND terminal_outcome IS NULL AND cancellation_state='none' AND last_sequence=?` (:110-120); lost race → retryable Conflict.
30: - AcknowledgeCancellation (`lifecycle.go:136-194`): fence-gated. Short-circuits (changed=false) when terminal or already acknowledged; state ≠ requested → Conflict; else inserts an ack `cancellation` event and CAS UPDATEs `cancellation_state='acknowledged', acknowledged_at` guarded by current_attempt match + state=requested + unchanged last_sequence (:156-181).
31: - `cancellation_state='uncertain'` exists in the schema enum and Health projection but no code path writes it (grep: only model.go definition + Health count sqlite.go:877).

33: ### 2.7 ProposeTerminal (`sqlite.go:722-807`)
34: The ONLY writer of terminal state (plus reconcileUnclaimed below). Validated proposal (outcome ∈ closed 7-value enum, reason/proposer bounded, :731-736). Immediate transaction: verifyFence → loadSnapshot; if Terminal already present, COMMIT the read tx and return (winner, won=false, nil) — losers observe the incumbent outcome instead of erroring (:753-758). Winner path: insert one `terminal` event at last_sequence+1 (payload {outcome,reason}) (:759-768), then CAS UPDATE runs setting lifecycle=outcome.Lifecycle(), liveness='terminal', finished_at, last_sequence, terminal_* columns `WHERE run_id=? AND current_attempt_id=? AND terminal_outcome IS NULL`; RowsAffected ≠ 1 → StaleFence loser (:769-786); attempts.outcome stamped on the winner's own attempt (:787-790); snapshot validated against the full terminal-consistency rules (model.go:355-364) before commit. Schema CHECK ties terminal_outcome ↔ finished_at ↔ terminal lifecycle (:268-269).

36: ### 2.8 Reconcile (`lifecycle.go:301-416`)

Pass 1 — unclaimed runs (`current_attempt_id IS NULL AND accepted_at older than grace`, :320-339): `reconcileUnclaimed` (:427-479) re-checks state in-tx, inserts one `terminal` event (attempt_id NULL) and CAS-terminalizes to interrupted/"owner_never_claimed_after_grace" guarded by `current_attempt_id IS NULL AND terminal_outcome IS NULL`; concurrent claim/win → silent no-op. Pass 2 — expired owners (runs joined to their current attempt where lease_expires_at older than grace, :360-383): probe recorded PID via ProcessProbe; `reconcileProcessDecision` matrix (:481-495):
38: - ErrProcessNotFound → interrupted, "owner_process_missing_after_grace";
39: - other probe error → cleanup_uncertain, "owner_process_identity_uncertain_after_grace";
40: - incomplete stored OR observed identity fields → cleanup_uncertain;
41: - exact field mismatch (host/boot/pid/birth) → interrupted, "owner_process_birth_mismatch_after_grace";
42: - exact live match → NO terminal: markStalled only (:497-509, liveness='stalled' CAS on still-current attempt; StaleFence tolerated).
43: Terminal proposals ride the DEAD attempt's own recorded fence (ProposedBy="reconciler"); ErrTerminal/ErrStaleFence from racing writers are tolerated (:392, :401). Every decision appended to reconciliation_log via recordReconciliation (:511-527; evidence reduced to class strings safe_identity_only / acceptance_timestamp_only; errors deliberately ignored by callers `_ = r.recordReconciliation(...)` :352, :411). Report counters Scanned/Terminal/Stalled/Uncertain + decisions list. Linux probe reads `/proc/<pid>/stat` starttime (field after last ')' index 19) as BirthToken + `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` as BootID + sha256(hostname)[:16] as HostDigest (process_linux.go:16-45, process.go:47-51); darwin uses sysctl kinfo start time + kern.boottime (process_darwin.go); other platforms return partial identity + ErrProcessIdentityUnavailable (process_other.go:16-18). PID ≤ 0 rejected. `NewProcessOwner` mints a random `own_…` ID and self-probes, tolerating identity unavailability by keeping PID only (process.go:30-45). Expiry comparisons use SQLite's clock in production: `julianday(col) <= julianday('now', '-<grace> seconds')` vs bound parameters when a Clock is injected (tests only; sqlite.go:1132-1144). Clock-jump safety pinned by test (backward jump never expires early, forward jump reconciles).

45: ### 2.9 Read paths
46: Snapshot (:594-606, loader :920-983) decodes one runs row with strict RFC3339Nano timestamps and correlation JSON (malformed → CodeCorrupt), then `Snapshot.Validate` (model.go:333-366: enums, UpdatedAt≥AcceptedAt, replay-boundary coherence oldest≤last+1, terminal↔finished↔lifecycle↔liveness consistency). Events (:809-854) pages ascending sequences after a cursor, limit default 200 max 512; payload/omission JSON decode failures are CodeCorrupt, not silently skipped. List (`lifecycle.go:196-266`) filters lifecycle/target/project/sprint/study with keyset cursor `(updated_at, run_id)` encoded as base64 JSON ≤1024 bytes, canonical RunID + parseable timestamp enforced (:278-291); each page row re-read as a full Snapshot. ReconciliationEvidence (:532-572) exposes newest-first decisions with evidence collapsed to the two allowlisted classes or "omitted".
47: 
48: ### 2.10 Command layer (`internal/app/run_commands.go`)
49: `runRepository` (:42-59) resolves the workspace, requires process-level runControlState, loads effective config, and fetches the per-process repository. Subcommands: list (:61-103), show (:105-129 — Snapshot rendered text or JSON), follow (:131-195 — poll Events 512-batch @250 ms when catching up else 1 s until `Lifecycle.IsTerminal() && after >= LastSequence`; ctx.Done returns nil, comment "Observation cancellation never changes the durable run"), cancel (:197-228 — canonical-reason whitelist, RequestCancellation, prints Changed flag), diagnostics (:230-276 — Health text/JSON + optional support export). Support export (:306-377) lists up to 50 runs, first 50 events each (sequence/type/omission only), ≤100 reconciliation evidence rows, ≤100 local log records; O_EXCL 0600 file, fsync, remove-on-failure, 1 MiB cap. Error mapping (:403-414): invalid_argument→ExitUsage, not_found→ExitValidation, conflict/terminal→ExitPartial, everything else→ExitRuntime.

51: ### 2.11 Production writers (detail owned by surface `durable-operation-spine`)

One Owner (`NewProcessOwner`) shared by all operations of the process.

58: Inputs: workspace root path; wall clock via SQLite `julianday('now')` (production) or injected Clock (tests); caller-supplied Target/Correlation/Owner/ProcessIdentity/Fence/EventDraft/TerminalProposal values (validated+bounded); agentwrap/OpenCode runtime events filtered through app-side `runtimeEventDraft` before reaching Append; operator CLI args (run-id, reason, flags); `/proc` or sysctl process metadata during probes. 60: ## 4. Authoritative state
61: 
62: - Database `.ultraplan/run-control.db` (DatabaseRelativePath, sqlite.go:22), schema v1 dual-recorded (`app_schema('run_control',1)` + PRAGMA user_version, :356-359):
